subject: Clarify: session retention, EU residency, and what gets persisted
messages:
From: Angela Kim <angela.kim@klarahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: what does Redwood keep from the session?

Hi Rafael —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Quick follow-up from our security and engineering teams — we want to be explicit about what Redwood will persist from user prompts and model outputs when we run inference. Example data that might appear in prompts: patient name, MRN, short clinical note snippets, and occasionally small binary attachments (images).

Questions:
- Does Redwood persist raw prompt text by default? If so, where and for how long?
- Are model outputs (generated text) kept separately from prompts? TTLs?
- Can we disable persistent storage for prompts (ephemeral sessions) for sensitive flows?
- Is there an EU-only processing option and EU key management (KMS)?
- What do your logs/audit trails contain (full prompt vs. metadata only)?

We want a short written answer we can share internally and a one-page diagram of the flow for our InfoSec review. I attached our short questionnaire (Klara_DQ.pdf).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we are trying to finalize provider decisions this quarter.

Thanks,
Angela
Security Liaison, Klara Health

---
Attachment: Klara_DQ.pdf (1 page, docx)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Angela Kim <angela.kim@klarahealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: what does Redwood keep from the session?

Hi Angela —

Thanks for the focused questions and for sending the questionnaire. High level answers below; Monica (CS) and Priyom (Solutions) are looped in to surface precise SLA/enterprise options. If helpful, we can put a 30-minute session on calendar with our Security Engineer to walk through the attached dataflow diagram and provide logged examples.

Short answers (defaults for Redwood hosted API):
- Default prompt retention: Redwood stores request payloads (raw prompts) for debugging and quality monitoring by default. Retention on hosted plans: 30 days.
- Generated outputs: stored separately from raw prompts; default retention 7 days for generated text on hosted.
- Ephemeral sessions: yes — we offer an "ephemeral mode" toggle that prevents persistent storage of raw prompts and outputs (session-kept only in-memory/KV cache); suitable for text-only sensitive flows.
- EU residency & KMS: we support EU-only processing regions; keys may be customer-managed via KMS in Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Logs & audit trails: default request logs include timestamps, route/model id, token counts, and an encrypted pointer to request payloads. Full-text prompt storage is only present when retention is enabled; audit logs can be configured to redact prompt text and retain metadata-only.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica will share the redwood dataflow diagram and a concise export sample so your InfoSec team can see field-level exports.
2) If you need EU KMS and custom TTLs beyond default, we can scope this as an enterprise option (Dedicated or Private).
3) Schedule a security call with engineering — Priyom will coordinate.

I'll highlight items in your questionnaire and send back a short written summary for your packet.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0192

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: what does Redwood keep from the session?

Hi Angela —

Attaching the dataflow diagram as promised and adding more concrete commitment options below. (Attachment: redwood-dataflow-diagram.svg)

Concrete options and defaults:
- Hosted (standard): prompts retained for 30 days; outputs retained for 7 days. Request and model identifiers are retained for 1 year for billing/usage analytics.
- Ephemeral mode (hosted): prompts and outputs not written to persistent storage. Session state lives only in-memory and is purged once the session ends or KV cache TTL elapses. Use case: high-sensitivity workflows (PHI).
- Dedicated/Private deployments: customer can opt for EU-only region, configure KMS with customer-managed keys, and set custom retention windows (including 0-day retention for persisted prompts).
- Audit logs: we can produce redactable exports. By default audit includes IP, timestamp, route, model version, token counts; full prompt text is only in the diagnostics export (protected).

Export formats: CSV/JSON with field-level redaction. Example export columns: request_id, timestamp, model_id, route, prompt_hash, prompt_text (optional), output_text (optional), region, retention_policy_id. We will share a sample export with fake data in the call.

Compliance artifacts: SOC2 report available (link below) and we can provide an executed DPA / DSA for EU controls.

Action items we can take this week:
- Provide redacted sample export (Monica)
- Provide SOC2 & DPA templates and confirm EU KMS options (Rafael)
- Set up 30-min security review this week (Priyom to propose times)

Regards,
Monica Patel

Hi all —

Thanks — that is very helpful. For our procurement and InfoSec checklist we would like the following finalized before contract signature:
- EU-only processing with EU KMS and confirmation that keys never leave the EU control plane.
- Default retention set to 30 days for prompts and 7 days for outputs unless ephemeral mode is enabled. We will request a 0-day option for PII-sensitive endpoints in Dedicated.
- A one-page export sample (redacted) showing the field names you listed.
- A copy of the DPA and SOC2 link for internal review.

Can you confirm you can provide a redacted sample export and the DPA by EOD Friday? Also please propose two time slots for the security review next week (we prefer mornings CET).

Appreciate the quick follow-up — we should be able to get approvals if the EU/KMS bit and export sample look good.

Thanks,
Angela
